#!/usr/bin/env bash
# sgt-dag-dispatch-hook — Stage hook called by dagr when a stage becomes ready.
#
# Calls sgt-dispatch with the given args, captures the fleet task ID,
# and writes dagr tracking files (dagr_run_id, dagr_stage_id) into every
# dispatched repo's fleet state directory so sgt-watch can auto-advance
# the DAG when the task completes.

trigger: an external DAG scheduler (dagr) reports one of its stages is ready to run
outcome: a normal dispatch happens and is durably tagged with which DAG run/stage it belongs to, so completion can be reported back
notes: dagr itself is an external tool this bin/ script defers to for ordering/dependency logic; Sergeant owns only the dispatch and the completion tagging.
rationale: The behavior — advance a multi-stage, dependency-ordered plan of dispatched work as stages complete — is exactly the branching/nested-workflow capability the proposal names as absent from the current engine (§7.7: 'True nested workflows do not exist yet'). Sergeant-rs delegates the whole capability to an external tool (dagr) rather than representing it; that delegation is itself the evidence a lower rung cannot cover this.
alternatives_considered: workflow (rejected: no bounded single-invocation outcome — the procedure spans an externally-scheduled multi-stage plan)

engine_gap.behavior: Advance a multi-stage plan of dispatched work units, where later stages become eligible only once their declared prerequisite stages complete, and completion of any stage must be durably attributable back to which plan/stage it satisfied.
engine_gap.source_evidence: sgt-dag-dispatch-hook and sgt-dag-run exist solely to bolt an external tool (dagr) onto sgt-dispatch/sgt-watch for exactly this purpose; every ordering, dependency, and advance-on-completion decision is made outside Sergeant.
lower_rungs_attempted: Represent the whole DAG as one ordinary workflow with several ordered stages (§6.2/§6.3)
Represent each DAG stage's dispatch as an actor stage invoking a shared helper (§6.5)
why_each_fails: A single workflow's stages run in one fixed, statically-authored sequence; a DAG's stages are dynamically gated on sibling completion across potentially many independently dispatched Works, which the current per-Work actor-stage engine has no way to express or observe.

A helper can dispatch one stage, but nothing in the engine owns 'which stages are now unblocked' as a durable fact recomputed from completion events — that ownership is exactly what dagr (external) supplies today.
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: The runtime must be able to own a durable multi-Work dependency graph (or delegate to and observe an external one) and re-evaluate readiness from Work-completion events, advancing dependent Works without an external polling script.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: Given a project YAML with a dag: block declaring stage B after stage A, dispatching the DAG results in only A running; when A's Work reaches a terminal done state, B is dispatched automatically without any operator or external-tool action, and the dependency is checkable from durable state alone.

notes: Directly parallel to proposal §4.4 'Procedure remains data' but applied to a capability class (branching/dependent multi-Work plans) the current sergeant-rs engine does not yet represent at all. (A11: mechanism noun normalized — the entry point is the script bin/sgt-dag-run.)

engine_gap.behavior: Declare a named, dependency-ordered set of stages (each producing its own dispatched Work) as data, and have the runtime create/track that structure and start it, dispatching only the stages whose dependencies are already satisfied.
engine_gap.source_evidence: The dag: YAML block is pure declarative data (stage names, repos, td/brief source, after: dependency edges) that sgt-dag-run and sgt-dag-dispatch-hook interpret only by handing it to the external dagr tool.
lower_rungs_attempted: Store the dependency graph as ordinary shared context (§6.6) consulted by an actor stage
Represent it as one long workflow whose stages are statically ordered by declaration order
why_each_fails: Shared context can hold the data, but nothing reads and enforces it without a scheduler; today that scheduler is the external dagr binary, not Sergeant.

engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: A project YAML dag: block with a fan-in dependency (two stages, both required by a third) results in the third stage's Work being dispatched only after both prerequisite Works reach a terminal done state, verifiable from durable engine state without consulting an external scheduler's own database.

engine_gap.behavior: A Work waiting on an externally-observable condition (a CI check's conclusion, a sibling Work's completion, an external task tracker's status, an arbitrary future timestamp) must be resumed automatically once that condition becomes true, with bounded jittered retry between checks, a hard deadline after which the wait fails outright, and an attempt-count ceiling after which the wait instead escalates to human input — all without any actor consuming a live turn while merely waiting.
engine_gap.source_evidence: bin/sgt-wake plus its condition-file convention (.sergeant-wake-condition) implement exactly this today as a stateless script re-invoked by an external scheduler (cron/dagr), storing attempt count, last-attempt timestamp, and next-not-before entirely as plain files in fleet state.
lower_rungs_attempted: Represent waiting as an ordinary actor stage that polls in a loop (§6.4/§6.5)
Represent it as a helper invoked by an external scheduler, as today's mechanism does (§6.5/§6.6)
why_each_fails: An actor stage that polls in a loop either burns a real model turn indefinitely (wasteful, and incompatible with the per-turn-process execution model D2 measured and shipped) or exits after one check, at which point retry/backoff/deadline state has nowhere durable to live except back in the runtime.

A helper re-invoked by an external scheduler works only as long as something outside Sergeant (cron, dagr) keeps re-invoking it, and the retry/backoff/deadline bookkeeping is then owned by loose files rather than by the runtime's own event-sourced Work state, so it cannot be recovered, queried, or reasoned about the way every other execution fact in sergeant-rs is (journal-as-only-truth, CLAUDE.md).
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: The runtime must be able to durably schedule a bounded, backoff-and-deadline-governed re-evaluation of an external condition for a specific Work, owning attempt count and next-eligible-time as journaled facts, and transition that Work automatically (met → resume, deadline exceeded → failed, max attempts → needs_input) without depending on an external scheduler to keep invoking anything.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: A Work is put into a waiting state with a github_check condition and a deadline; without any external cron job running, the daemon itself re-evaluates the condition on a bounded schedule, resumes the Work automatically the first time the check reports success, and if the deadline passes first, the Work is observed (via the API) to have failed with 'deadline exceeded' — all reconstructable from the journal alone.

# distinguishing "not closed yet" from "could not be looked up".
_require_owning_td_task_closed() {
  local repo_dir="$1" repo_name="$2" status="$3"
  local lookup=0 state

  state="$(_owning_td_task_state "$repo_dir" "$repo_name")" || lookup=$?
  case "$lookup" in
    0)
      [[ "$state" == "closed" ]] || \
        _die "$repo_name is not terminal: $status; owning td task is $state"
      ;;
    2) _die "$state" ;;
